stages.name: Value Analysis
stages.objective: Quantify value delivered by product to customers
stages.input: Customer data, ROI studies, industry benchmarks
stages.output: Value assessment framework with value drivers
stages.activities: Analyze customer financial outcomes, identify value drivers by segment, quantify time savings, quantify cost reductions, quantify revenue increases
stages.tools: Financial analysis, ROI models, value frameworks
stages.successMetric: Value framework with 3-5 value drivers documented
stages.decisionPoints: Value drivers clear? Quantifiable? Customer-validated? Segment variations?
stages.qualityGate: Value analysis complete, drivers validated by sales/customers

stages.name: Willingness-to-Pay Research
stages.objective: Understand what customers will pay for product
stages.input: Value analysis, customer segments, competitive offerings
stages.activities: Conduct customer interviews, analyze historical pricing responses, test pricing elasticity, segment by value perception, identify price sensitivity
stages.decisionPoints: Price sensitivity understood? Willingness clear? Variations by segment? Optimal price identified?
stages.qualityGate: Willingness-to-pay research complete, price ranges identified

stages.name: Pricing Model Development
stages.objective: Design pricing model reflecting value delivered
stages.input: Value analysis, willingness-to-pay, business model
stages.activities: Design pricing approach (value-based, usage-based, tiering), model financial impact, assess competitive positioning, model revenue impact, document assumptions
stages.successMetric: Pricing model designed with financial modeling complete
stages.decisionPoints: Model reflects value? Financial impact acceptable? Competitive positioning? Sales willing to sell?
stages.qualityGate: Pricing model approved, economic model validated

stages.name: Competitive Benchmarking
stages.objective: Validate pricing against competitive offerings
stages.input: Competitor pricing, competitor features, value positioning
stages.activities: Research competitor pricing, assess feature/value comparison, identify price positioning (premium/parity/discount), assess customer perception
stages.decisionPoints: Pricing premium justified? Value perception clear? Competitive differentiation evident?

stages.name: Test & Validation
stages.objective: Test pricing model before full launch
stages.input: Proposed pricing model, test customers, sales process
stages.output: Validated pricing model with customer feedback
stages.activities: Test with select customers, measure price acceptance, measure sales cycle impact, gather qualitative feedback, refine model based on learning
stages.successMetric: Pricing tested with 10-20 customers, acceptance validated
stages.decisionPoints: Customers accept pricing? Sales adoption? Messaging clear? Objections identified?
stages.qualityGate: Pricing validated, sales team confident, launch ready

stages.name: Customer Segmentation for Packaging
stages.objective: Identify distinct customer segments for separate product tiers
stages.input: Customer data, use case analysis, revenue data
stages.activities: Segment customers by use case, segment by company size, segment by value perception, assess willingness to pay variations, identify tier boundaries
stages.successMetric: 3-4 distinct segments identified with tier potential
stages.decisionPoints: Segments distinct? Separate use cases? Pricing variations justified?
stages.qualityGate: Segment definition finalized, tier structure proposed

stages.name: Feature Mapping & Tier Definition
stages.objective: Map features to tiers and define each tier clearly
stages.input: Feature roadmap, segment use cases, competitive tiers
stages.activities: Map features to each tier, define differentiators between tiers, establish feature upgrade paths, ensure tier appeal for each segment
stages.successMetric: 3-4 tiers defined with clear feature differentiation
stages.decisionPoints: Tiers distinct? Feature allocation optimal? Upgrade paths clear? Pricing justified?
stages.qualityGate: Tier definitions approved, feature mapping validated

stages.name: Pricing Structure & Tier Economics
stages.objective: Price each tier and model economics
stages.input: Tier definitions, value analysis, competitive pricing
stages.activities: Price each tier based on value, model revenue impact by tier, assess cannibalization risk, model growth trajectory, identify margin implications
stages.successMetric: Pricing structure with financial model complete
stages.decisionPoints: Price gaps appropriate? Revenue modeling realistic? Margins acceptable?
stages.qualityGate: Tier pricing approved, financial model validated

stages.name: Messaging & Positioning
stages.objective: Create compelling messaging for each tier
stages.input: Tier definitions, value propositions, segment needs
stages.activities: Develop tier naming, create tier value props, develop comparison messaging, create upgrade paths narrative, identify target buyers per tier
stages.successMetric: Tier messaging developed for all tiers
stages.decisionPoints: Messaging clear? Differentiation evident? Customer-resonant? Upgrade paths enticing?

stages.name: Add-On & Module Identification
stages.objective: Identify potential add-on products and modules
stages.input: Product roadmap, customer requests, competitive offerings
stages.activities: Analyze customer expansion requests, identify product gaps, research competitor add-ons, assess technical feasibility, prioritize by demand
stages.decisionPoints: Add-ons valuable? Technical feasible? Market demand?

stages.name: Value Assessment & Willingness to Pay
stages.objective: Quantify value and price sensitivity for add-ons
stages.input: Add-on descriptions, customer data, use cases
stages.activities: Analyze customer willingness to pay, quantify value per segment, assess price sensitivity, estimate addressable market
stages.successMetric: Value and pricing assessed for all add-ons
stages.decisionPoints: Value clear? WTP realistic? Pricing opportunities?

stages.name: Add-On Packaging & Bundling
stages.objective: Design packaging and bundling strategies
stages.input: Add-ons identified, pricing data, customer segments
stages.activities: Design standalone vs. bundled options, identify bundling themes, assess bundling ROI, plan upgrade paths
stages.decisionPoints: Packaging resonant? Bundling opportunities? Cannibalization risk?

stages.name: Pricing Model Development
stages.objective: Develop pricing for add-on products
stages.input: Packaging strategy, value assessment, competitive pricing
stages.activities: Price standalone options, price bundled options, model revenue impact, set discount policies, model margin impact
stages.decisionPoints: Pricing competitive? Revenue modeling realistic? Margins acceptable?
stages.qualityGate: Pricing approved and ready for launch

stages.name: Sales & Marketing Enablement
stages.objective: Enable sales and marketing to sell add-ons
stages.input: Add-on pricing, packaging, business case
stages.activities: Train sales on add-ons, create marketing materials, develop add-on positioning, identify target buyers, create bundling recommendations
stages.successMetric: Sales and marketing trained and equipped
stages.decisionPoints: Team confident? Materials compelling? Positioning clear?

stages.name: Add-On Launch & Go-to-Market
stages.objective: Launch add-ons to market
stages.input: Pricing, sales enablement, marketing plan
stages.activities: Announce add-ons, execute marketing campaign, support sales efforts, track adoption, gather feedback
stages.decisionPoints: Launch smooth? Adoption rates healthy? Customer reaction positive?
stages.qualityGate: Add-ons in market with tracking active

stages.name: Hypothesis Development
stages.objective: Define what pricing hypothesis to test
stages.input: Pricing concerns, customer feedback, competitive data
stages.output: Clear test hypothesis with success metrics
stages.activities: Identify pricing question to answer, develop hypothesis, define primary metric, define success threshold, estimate sample size needed
stages.decisionPoints: Hypothesis clear? Metric meaningful? Sample size adequate?

stages.name: Test Design & Setup
stages.objective: Design pricing test
stages.input: Hypothesis, pricing options, customer segments
stages.activities: Design test structure (A/B, multivariate), select test variables, identify test audience, plan control group, design randomization
stages.decisionPoints: Test design rigorous? Control group appropriate? Randomization sound?

stages.name: Test Implementation & Launch
stages.objective: Launch pricing test
stages.input: Test design, pricing options
stages.output: Test active with control and test groups
stages.activities: Set up test in platform, configure pricing variations, randomize customer assignments, track implementation
stages.decisionPoints: Randomization working? Groups balanced? Tracking accurate?

stages.name: Data Collection & Monitoring
stages.objective: Collect test data and monitor progress
stages.input: Test active, customer interactions
stages.activities: Monitor test progress, check for issues, collect response data, monitor for bias, track statistical power
stages.decisionPoints: Data quality good? Sufficient sample? Time to run test?

stages.name: Results Analysis & Statistical Testing
stages.objective: Analyze test results statistically
stages.input: Test data, control and test groups
stages.activities: Run statistical tests, calculate effect sizes, assess significance, analyze by segment, identify learnings
stages.decisionPoints: Results significant? Effect size meaningful? Learnings clear?

stages.name: Recommendation & Decision
stages.objective: Develop recommendation based on results
stages.input: Analysis results, business implications
stages.activities: Develop recommendation (change, don't change, test more), model business impact, assess risk, present to leadership
stages.decisionPoints: Recommendation clear? Business impact quantified? Risk assessed?

stages.name: Rollout & Impact Monitoring
stages.objective: Implement decision and monitor impact
stages.input: Leadership decision, implementation plan
stages.activities: Implement pricing change or run next test, monitor impact on revenue, monitor customer satisfaction, track adoption
stages.decisionPoints: Implementation smooth? Impact as expected?

stages.name: Pricing Increase Justification
stages.objective: Develop business justification for price increase
stages.input: Cost structure, market conditions, competitor pricing, value delivered
stages.activities: Analyze cost inflation, assess value delivered, benchmark against competitors, quantify justification, identify timing
stages.decisionPoints: Justification compelling? Timing right? Value clear?

stages.name: Customer Impact Analysis
stages.objective: Assess impact of increase on customer segments
stages.input: Pricing increase, customer list, contract terms
stages.output: Segmented impact analysis with risk assessment
stages.activities: Segment customers by renewal date, assess increase impact per segment, identify churn risk, calculate revenue impact, identify negotiation cases
stages.successMetric: Impact analyzed by segment with risk identified
stages.decisionPoints: Impact manageable? Churn risk acceptable? Revenue impact positive?

stages.name: Tiered Implementation Strategy
stages.objective: Develop strategy for phased price increase
stages.input: Impact analysis, customer risk tiers
stages.activities: Define increase amount by segment, plan effective date, identify negotiation strategy for at-risk accounts, plan communication timeline
stages.decisionPoints: Tiers meaningful? Timing logical? Negotiation approach clear?

stages.name: Communication Planning
stages.objective: Plan communication strategy for price increase
stages.input: Tiered strategy, messaging approach
stages.activities: Draft customer communication, prepare sales talking points, prepare customer success messaging, develop Q&A, plan escalation path
stages.decisionPoints: Messaging positive? Justification clear? Support adequate?

stages.name: Price Increase Implementation
stages.objective: Execute price increase across customer base
stages.input: Communication plan, tiered strategy
stages.output: Price increase implemented with customer communication
stages.activities: Send customer communications, support sales/CSM conversations, process negotiated deals, update billing systems, monitor customer reaction
stages.successMetric: Increase communicated, billing updated for all customers
stages.decisionPoints: Communication received well? Churn risk realized? Negotiated deals within tolerance?

stages.name: Renewal & Negotiation Management
stages.objective: Manage renewals post-price increase
stages.input: Customer communication, negotiation strategy
stages.activities: Handle price increase objections, negotiate with at-risk accounts, close renewals, document learnings
stages.decisionPoints: Churn rate acceptable? Negotiated discounts within budget?

stages.name: Results Monitoring & Optimization
stages.objective: Monitor impact and optimize approach
stages.input: Renewal results, churn data, revenue impact
stages.activities: Track actual churn vs. projection, calculate revenue impact, gather customer feedback, identify learnings for future increases
stages.decisionPoints: Impact as expected? Learnings captured? Strategy improved?
stages.qualityGate: Learnings applied to future pricing decisions

stages.name: Renewal Pricing Analysis
stages.objective: Analyze historical renewal pricing patterns
stages.input: Renewal data, customer history, pricing by segment
stages.activities: Analyze historical renewal price changes, segment by customer type, identify escalation patterns, assess elasticity, identify opportunities
stages.decisionPoints: Patterns clear? Escalation opportunities? Risk identified?

stages.name: Escalation Strategy Development
stages.objective: Develop renewal escalation strategy
stages.input: Pricing analysis, competitive pricing, market conditions
stages.activities: Define escalation approach (annual increases, usage-based, market-based), set escalation rates by segment, identify negotiation boundaries
stages.decisionPoints: Strategy realistic? Competitive? Acceptable to customers?

stages.name: Segment-Specific Escalation Plans
stages.objective: Develop customized escalation for each customer segment
stages.input: Escalation strategy, customer segments
stages.activities: Develop tiered pricing by segment, identify at-risk customers, plan negotiation thresholds, prepare sales guidance
stages.decisionPoints: Differentiation meaningful? Fair pricing? Competitive?

stages.name: Communication & Sales Preparation
stages.objective: Prepare sales team for renewal pricing conversations
stages.input: Escalation strategy, customer-specific pricing
stages.output: Trained sales team ready for conversations
stages.activities: Train sales on escalation rationale, provide customer talking points, provide negotiation guidance, distribute pricing sheets, practice objection handling
stages.tools: Training materials, talking points, negotiation guides
stages.decisionPoints: Team confident? Messaging clear? Objection handling ready?

stages.name: Renewal Pricing Negotiation
stages.objective: Negotiate renewal pricing with customers
stages.input: Escalation strategy, customer-specific pricing, negotiation guidance
stages.activities: Present pricing, explain rationale, address objections, negotiate within guidelines, close renewals
stages.successMetric: Renewals closed at target pricing or better
stages.decisionPoints: Pricing accepted? Negotiations within tolerance? Customer satisfied?

stages.name: Results Monitoring & Analysis
stages.objective: Monitor renewal pricing results
stages.input: Renewal agreements, pricing achieved
stages.activities: Track average pricing achieved vs. target, segment performance, analyze negotiated discounts, calculate revenue impact
stages.decisionPoints: Targets met? Discount rates acceptable? Revenue impact positive?

stages.name: Continuous Optimization
stages.objective: Optimize renewal pricing strategy
stages.input: Results data, customer feedback, market changes
stages.activities: Analyze what worked, identify improvements, adjust escalation rates, update customer communication, plan next cycle
stages.decisionPoints: Learnings captured? Strategy improved? Prepared for next cycle?
